entities.title: Godot's engine served in parts
entities.summary: build.mjs cuts index.wasm into 20 MiB parts and the Worker joins them.
entities.context: Godot's WebAssembly engine is about 39.5 MB; Cloudflare serves static files of at most 25 MiB.
entities.decision: Store index.wasm.0, .1, … as static assets and stream them back as one index.wasm from the Worker, which runs first for that path.
entities.rationale: Keeps the stock Godot loader, which asks for index.wasm, unchanged.

entities.title: Playing the computer without signing in
entities.summary: The GDD keeps playing the computer without an account; the Worker now needs a sign-in for the page.
entities.context: GDD pillar 2 says the computer needs no account, and the decision log kept playing the computer without signing in ("Claude, open for the owner"). Since Gambit moved to icelander.net's one sign-in, the Worker serves the page only to players signed in with games:play, so a signed-out visitor never reaches the computer; the client still has its signed-out paths: the sign-in card, and a history kept on the device.

options.title: Keep the sign-in for the whole game
options.consequences: Pillar 2 and the README's "on the device otherwise" change; the signed-out paths in the client could go.

options.title: Serve the page signed out, for the computer only
options.consequences: index.ts lets the page through without a sign-in; the API already answers /me signed out, and everything else stays behind the sign-in.

entities.title: What the first version's features became
entities.summary: Pass and play on one screen, and adding contacts by hand, were dropped.
entities.context: The decision log keeps the Worker, D1 and a Durable Object per game, and Stockfish at eight strengths, from the first version, and drops pass & play on one screen and adding contacts by hand. It is marked "Claude, open for the owner".

entities.title: The name Gambit, the path chess
entities.summary: Working title Gambit; the slug and path stay chess.
entities.context: The decision log names the game Gambit and keeps the slug and path chess (/games/retro/chess), marked "Claude, open for the owner". Everything technical (the folder, the Worker, the database, BASE) is chess.

entities.title: No clocks; email only for new invitations
entities.summary: Games are correspondence-style, without clocks, and only new invitations are emailed.
entities.context: The decision log says no clocks (correspondence-style games) and email only for new invitations, not for each move, marked "Claude, open for the owner". The non-goals list clocks, ratings, spectators, puzzles, engine analysis, move notifications and phone-sized layouts "for now".
